The generalization gap emerges because this corruption preferentially distorts updates in directions of high curvature (where gradients change fastest between parameter versions), causing the model to over-exploit low-curvature flat directions that generalize poorly, while under-exploiting sharp minima structure that might generalize better or converge more cleanly. In fine-tuning specifically, where the loss landscape is already carved by pretraining and small gradient magnitudes matter enormously for preserving useful representations, even modest momentum corruption can cause irreversible drift in layer-wise update ratios — the optimizer effectively "forgets" the curvature structure that made the pretrained features worth preserving.
